questions.question: How much of the world's land surface did the British Empire govern at its height?
questions.explanation: At its height, the British Empire governed nearly a quarter of the world's land surface and about a fifth of its population, spreading English globally.

questions.question: What was the primary force behind English becoming the global language in the 20th century?
questions.explanation: While the British Empire spread English earlier, American dominance in economics, technology, film, and music drove English's global status in the 20th century.

questions.question: Why is English important in aviation?
options: It is the standard international language of air traffic control
Planes are mostly built in England
Pilots are required to be native speakers
questions.explanation: English is the official international language of civil aviation: pilots and air traffic controllers on international flights communicate in English.

questions.question: What role does English play in modern science?
options: It is the dominant language of international research publication
It is banned in most journals
It is used only in British universities
questions.explanation: The vast majority of international scientific papers are published in English, making it the working language of global research.

questions.question: In what way did colonialism spread English differently in settler colonies versus exploitation colonies?
options: In settler colonies English became the majority native language; in exploitation colonies it became an elite or administrative language
Exploitation colonies all became Inner Circle countries
There was no difference at all
questions.explanation: In settler colonies like Australia and Canada, English speakers displaced local populations and English became native; in colonies like India and Nigeria, it became the language of administration and education.
